checks.description: A valid signature binds the current job ID, descriptor hash and fresh per-invocation challenge; unavailable randomness fails closed.
Forged, modified, wrong-key, wrong-job, stale, replayed, truncated and malformed receipts refuse before target open or modification.
Durable one-shot claim is published before receipt signing; duplicates and lost acknowledgements remain consumed without retry or rearm.
Synthetic QEMU full/fault/abrupt tests and default diagnostic regression pass; crypto provenance and size/layout are recorded; output stays nonbootable and nondeployable.

constraints.text: Retain recorded Ed25519 source, version, license, ARM64 static build method and measured binary/root and memory impact. If integration cannot fit the reviewed guest and 8 GB geometry, stop with measurements and an alternative for review. Do not add handwritten cryptography or silently change license terms.

Keep a dedicated receipt verification key pinned in the inert candidate and signing material in ignored host-side provisioning. Public synthetic keys cannot authenticate a physical claim. Verify canonical versioned bytes, strict response framing, signature and exact current job, descriptor and challenge before target open; retain forged and replay tests.

Sign only after consumed state and its containing directory are durably synced. Signing, transport or persistence uncertainty leaves the claim consumed without automatic retry or rearm; retain interruption and lost-response checks.

Keep source hashes for changed implementation files in delivery evidence despite their removal from immutable requirements. Preserve the read-only default diagnostic and nonbootable, nondeployable candidate. H12 still requires live identity, reviewed physical artifact and operation, recovery and a separate high-consequence review before any write.

decision.rationale: This is a bounded workflow-record correction. The proposal and four acceptance checks are unchanged. The removed requirements are implementation files that the approved task had to modify; pinning their pre-implementation hashes as immutable requirements incorrectly invalidated completion. The six remaining documents are stable governing requirements, and their current hashes match the review context. Integrated commit a1c89b6 records the Monocypher 4.0.3 provenance, measured 2,888-byte writer increase and 3,806-byte NFS-root increase, and synthetic QEMU evidence; that evidence remains subject to separate delivery verification. Removing implementation files from the requirements snapshot must not remove their source hashes from delivery evidence. This approval concerns only the offline authenticated-claim task and grants no physical construction, provisioning, write, boot-policy or release authority.

evidence.limitations: All evidence is offline and synthetic. No printer, physical eMMC, H616 boot chain, production signer provisioning, bootable SD, live CID/dev_t mapping, physical power-loss recovery, or release behavior was tested. Test signing key is synthetic public test material. Network claim preemption can still deny service but cannot forge an accepted receipt.
evidence.method: Native C/server tests accepted a valid receipt over a fresh random challenge and refused when getrandom was unavailable. Beelink private-namespace QEMU valid claim-only case verified the signed receipt, durably consumed the claim, and did not open the target.
evidence.profile: Synthetic H616/QEMU commissioning fixture on Beelink; no connected printer profile
